# LFDT Lab owner approval package

Status: READY-FOR-OWNER-APPROVAL. No submission, membership or acceptance is claimed.

Current primary process: https://github.com/LF-Decentralized-Trust/lab-proposals
Form: https://github.com/LF-Decentralized-Trust/lab-proposals/issues/new?template=lab-proposal.yml

The current repository README replaces the older manual proposal PR with a **Lab Proposal issue form**. Do not send an obsolete PR. Review submission.md against that form; use the technical summary and governance readiness attachments. Owner must provide real initial human committer/contact URLs, confirm the submitting entity, approve proposed scope and any asset-transfer authority. Keep personal information private unless the owner explicitly chooses a public contact route.

A Lab proposal does not require buying membership. Code is Apache-2.0 with DCO; specification work has a different CSL framework. This proposal is software, not a normative national or payment specification. If admitted, LFDT coordinates repository/naming/asset onboarding; transfer nothing pre-approval.

## Current entry route verified during close-out

The current Labs README explicitly retires the proposal-fork/PR process. Use https://github.com/LF-Decentralized-Trust/lab-proposals/issues/new?template=lab-proposal.yml after establishing fit and contributor authority. The live README requires Apache-2.0 code with DCO-signed imports, flags names based on existing products, and coordinates asset transfers only after acceptance. MessageBench’s ancillary XSD terms and existing unsigned history must be disclosed; no hosting eligibility or trademark/IP transfer is presumed. First send the nonbinding scope question through the authorized corporate channel. Source: https://github.com/LF-Decentralized-Trust/lab-proposals/blob/main/README.md .
